claim.markdown_says: Lines 37076-37090 place every one of these at column 0: 'b) If argument-1 is alphanumeric, ...', 'c) ...', 'd) ...', 'e) ...', 'f) ...', '5) If the LOCALE keyword is specified, the following rules apply:', 'a) Locale-name-1, ...', 'b) The content of argument-1 ...' - while the matching item on the previous page is indented ('   a) Argument-1 shall have one of the following two formats:', line 37054)
claim.why_it_matters: The lettered sub-rules are detached from their parent numbered rule at the page boundary, so in the markdown b)-f) read as peers of 5) rather than as continuations of 4). A reader (or a tool citing 15.68.3 rule 4) b)) cannot tell which numbered rule a lettered sub-rule qualifies, and the transcription is internally inconsistent with the same list's item a) on p. 925.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED - the difference is leading whitespace only; no content is missing, reordered, or misattributed, and the rule hierarchy is not ambiguous.

1. TEXT IS COMPLETE AND CORRECT. I rendered spec_p926.png at 300 dpi and read it against specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 37065-37090. Every item on the page is present in the markdown, in the printed order, with the correct label and verbatim wording: the format line and its trailing '[ space-string ]', the 'where' block with its three em-dash definitions, b) alphanumeric CR/DB, c) national CR/DB, d) decimal/grouping separator and DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, e) leading/trailing spaces ignored, f) ANYCASE matching via LOWER-CASE, 5) 'If the LOCALE keyword is specified, the following rules apply:', a) locale-name-1 / LC_MONETARY / EC-LOCALE-MISSING, b) content of argument-1 consistent with LC_MONETARY. Nothing is dropped and nothing is moved between parents. The kind label 'misplaced-content' is therefore wrong on its face: the content is exactly where the PDF puts it in reading order.

2. THE PDF INDENTATION IS AS CLAIMED, AND THE MARKDOWN FLATTENING IS AS CLAIMED. In the rendered page, '5)' sits at the left rule margin while 'b)' through 'f)' and the two items following 5) sit one indent level to the right, matching the indent of 'a) Argument-1 shall have one of the following two formats:' on p. 925. In the markdown those eight lines carry zero leading spaces (verified with cat -A), while p. 925's 'a)' carries a 3-space indent. Both halves of the claim's observation are factually accurate. What fails is the inference drawn from them.

3. THE NESTING IS NOT LOST - IT IS ENCODED IN THE LABEL ALPHABET, WHICH IS 100% CONSISTENT. Across the whole transcription, numbered rule items appear at column 0 in 4039 of 4039 cases and are NEVER indented. Lettered sub-items appear at column 0 in 572 cases and indented in 794. So a lettered item can never be confused with a numbered item on the basis of column, because column 0 is the universal, exceptionless home of numbered items. A reader or tool sees '4) ... a) ... b) ... f) ... 5) ... a) ... b)'; the letter series restarting at a) immediately after each numbered parent that ends in 'the following rules apply:' makes the tree unambiguously recoverable. The claim's core assertion - 'b)-f) read as peers of 5)' - does not hold: 'b)' and '5)' are drawn from disjoint label alphabets and can never be siblings in an ISO rule list.

4. THE INCONSISTENCY IS A DOCUMENT-WIDE STYLISTIC VARIATION, NOT A PAGE-926 DEFECT. The flat-lettering style occurs on 167 distinct pages and the indented style on 227; only 17 pages mix the two internally, and page 926 is not one of them (all its lettered items are flat, uniformly). Page 925 is likewise internally uniform. The 'internal inconsistency' the claim names is therefore a boundary between two pages transcribed under different whitespace conventions - the same class of artifact as page-break furniture - and flagging it here would require flagging roughly 170 pages identically.

5. MEANING IS UNCHANGED. Nothing about which numbered rule governs which lettered sub-rule differs between the two sources; only the visual depth cue does. Under the rejection criteria this is formatting that does not change meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The PDF does indent b)-f) under rule 4) and a)-b) under rule 5), and specs/ISO_COBOL.md does render all eight at column 0 while p. 925's item a) carries a 3-space indent - but all text, labels and ordering are verbatim identical, and the list hierarchy remains unambiguous because numbered items occupy column 0 in 4039/4039 cases document-wide while lettered series restart at a) under each numbered parent. The flat-vs-indented split is a transcription whitespace convention that varies by page (167 flat pages vs 227 indented, only 17 mixed), not a defect local to page 926. If the ledger wants uniform list indentation it is a global cosmetic normalization task, not a per-page structural finding.
